draft.title: String to Integer Conversion
draft.statement:
Parse the input string `s` and produce a signed 32‑bit integer following these steps:

* Skip any leading space characters.
* Look at the next character: if it is ‘-’ or ‘+’, record the sign (negative for ‘-’, positive otherwise) and move past it.
* Read consecutive digits, ignoring any leading zeros, until a non‑digit or the end of the string appears. If no digit is read, the result is 0.
* Clamp the obtained value to the range **[-2³¹, 2³¹‑1]**. Values smaller than -2³¹ become -2³¹, larger than 2³¹‑1 become 2³¹‑1.

Return the final integer.
constraints: s contains only letters, digits, space, '+', '-', and '.'

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Identify the exact point where digit reading should stop and handle overflow before it occurs.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Iterate through the string character by character, building the number using a big‑integer type, then clamp at the end – O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
mentorNotes.optimal: Process characters once, updating the result while checking overflow on each step – O(n) time, O(1) space.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to skip leading spaces before checking sign
Treating characters after the first non‑digit as part of the number
Missing overflow detection for the last digit
Returning the sign incorrectly when no digits are found
